clue.text: Impractical person is absorbed by silly detail

indicators.note: being absorbed by something means being taken right inside it, so one piece sits within the other
silly suggests the letters of the following word behaving foolishly and getting jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with their head in the clouds gets lost in a trivial detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' makes IDEALT from the clue's six-letter word; 'is absorbed by' looks like the definition's verb, but it sets the two-letter word inside that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues perfect principles over workable reality, so is commonly called impractical.

clue.text: Flag seen when ship crosses river

indicators.note: a vessel crossing a river has the river running through it in this picture, so one piece is set within the other

parts.note: a steamer is a kind of ship

explanation.surface: A banner is visible as a vessel makes its way over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow pennant flown from a mast, a type of flag.

clue.text: Passes on skills to mischief-maker

indicators.note: to here means added on to, so the skills follow the mischief-maker in the answer

parts.note: an imp is a little devil who makes mischief
arts are skills, as in the arts of persuasion

explanation.surface: Someone hands down their talents to a young rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart is to transmit or communicate knowledge, a synonym of handing it along.

clue.text: Socialist — super Scot?

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, means super or great
Ian is a typically Scottish first name, the crossword's stock Scot

explanation.surface: Is a left-winger a marvellous Scotsman?
explanation.walkthrough: The Fabian Society is a long-standing British socialist organisation favouring gradual reform.
explanation.definitionFit: A Fabian is a member of the Fabian Society, a British group advocating gradual socialism.

clue.text: Measure vehicle, the man needing length

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up a coach while the driver wants extra length.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushel is an old unit of dry volume for grain and fruit, used as a measure.

clue.text: Mate aroused me terribly — beautifully fitting garment being this?

indicators.note: terribly suggests the words before it are thrown into disorder, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's partner was thrilled by a perfectly tailored outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges the letters of MATE AROUSED ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing cut to an individual's own dimensions by a tailor is described this way, hence its fine fit.

clue.text: Sun gone? Now you can go back to work

definitions.text: Sun gone? Now you can go back to work

parts.words: Sun gone? Now you can go back to work
parts.note: Sun is the usual short form of a day of the week, not the star; once that day is over the working week begins again

explanation.surface: With the sunshine gone, it is time to return to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: Sun looks like the star setting, but it is the abbreviation of Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: The start of the week, when weekend ends and people return to their jobs.

clue.text: Item of furniture needed for the final sitting

definitions.text: Item of furniture needed for the final sitting

parts.words: Item of furniture needed for the final sitting
parts.note: a seat used for an execution, where the condemned sits for the last time

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture is wanted for a last session in front of a portrait painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Final sitting sounds like a last portrait session or meal, but it is an execution.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat wired to carry a lethal current, used in some American states for executions.

clue.text: Disquiet of a Parisian female when meeting English

parts.note: une is the French feminine word for a, as a Parisian would say it of a female noun
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman feels anxious on encountering an Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: Unease is a feeling of anxiety or discomfort, a synonym of disquiet.

clue.text: Burning boy got down

parts.note: alight means on fire or burning
Ed is a short boy's name, from Edward

explanation.surface: A boy on fire jumped to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to dismount or descend from a vehicle, so alighted means descended.

clue.text: Tune that's fine but not loud

indicators.note: but not here means the following thing is to be left out of the word before it

parts.note: fair can mean fine, as in fair weather
F stands for forte, the musical direction meaning loud

explanation.surface: A melody is acceptable as long as it is not played noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: F is forte, loud in music notation.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a melody or song, a synonym of tune.

clue.text: Hospital suppliers can make a meal of it

definitions.text: Hospital suppliers can make a meal of it

parts.words: Hospital suppliers can make a meal of it
parts.note: an element is swallowed in a drink before an X-ray, the preparation called a meal by radiographers

explanation.surface: Those providing for a hospital can cook up a dinner from it.
explanation.walkthrough: Making a meal of something means fussing over it, but here a barium meal is the drink taken before an X-ray.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical element whose sulphate is swallowed as a contrast medium so the gut shows on X-rays.

clue.text: Sheet metal in place inside gallery

indicators.note: inside places the preceding words within the gallery that follows

parts.note: the Tate is a famous group of London art galleries
taken as written
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A metal panel is put in position within an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British art galleries, the crossword's stock gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinplate is thin steel sheet coated with tin, a form of sheet metal.

clue.text: Father and son dance

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
S is the standard abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A dad and his boy take to the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas is a step or short dance in ballet, as in pas de deux.

clue.text: A maiden and a politician becoming romantic

parts.note: taken as written
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A young woman and an MP are falling in love.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY is a member of Britain's Conservative Party; M for maiden comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatory describes things relating to sexual love, as in amatory verse.

clue.text: It's all right to hug a tree

indicators.note: to hug is to hold closely in one's arms, so the outer word wraps around the letter

parts.note: OK means it is all right
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is fine to embrace a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The oak is a common broadleaf tree bearing acorns.

clue.text: Don't indulge — you'll get a black mark!

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a stain is a mark or blemish

explanation.surface: Resist temptation, or you will earn a demerit.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from something pleasurable such as drink, which is not indulging.

clue.text: South of stream hawk becomes exhausted

indicators.note: in a down answer, south of means placed below, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a burn is a Scottish word for a stream
to hawk goods is to sell them aggressively, the same as tout

explanation.surface: A bird of prey down by a brook becomes tired out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South of' puts TOUT below BURN in this down entry. BURN is Scottish for a small stream; hawk here is the verb meaning to peddle, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt out describes someone worn out from overwork, so it means utterly exhausted.

clue.text: Bear gets to rat-infested shelter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a place infested by vermin has them inside it, so the creature goes within the shelter word

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind, as in the lee of a wall
taken as written

explanation.surface: A person puts up with a shelter overrun by rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'rat-infested' hides the split: the rodent is fodder and 'infested' the container signal. Bear is the verb endure, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to endure or put up with it, a synonym of tolerate.

clue.text: Tragic character — nothing over time he will love

parts.note: O looks like zero, meaning nothing
he'll is the contraction of he will, written without the apostrophe
love means zero in tennis scoring, written O

explanation.surface: A figure from tragedy: with nothing left over time, he will be in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link in this down clue; love is O from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Moor of Venice, who kills his wife from jealousy, is a classic tragic hero.

clue.text: Fool taking one drug after another

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine, one illegal drug
pot is cannabis, another drug

explanation.surface: A foolish person uses one narcotic after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or crazy person, a synonym of fool.

clue.text: Restrictions at home circumvented by Charles

indicators.note: circumvented by means surrounded by, so the first piece sits within the name

parts.note: Chas is a short form of the name Charles
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Charles finds ways round the rules on staying in.
explanation.definitionFit: Chains are fetters, and figuratively anything that restricts freedom.

clue.text: Modern movement provides interest outside work

indicators.note: outside means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: a part, as in a share or stake, is an interest in something
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A new trend gives a stake beyond employment.
explanation.walkthrough: Work as opus is a crossword convention; interest means a share or stake, not curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1950s-60s art movement using images from advertising and comics, a modern artistic movement.

clue.text: Things left behind destroyed by slicer

indicators.note: destroyed suggests the word after it is wrecked, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Leftovers ruined by a kitchen slicer.
explanation.definitionFit: Relics are survivals or remains from an earlier time, things that are left over.

clue.text: Bird subsequently getting head chopped off

indicators.note: having its head chopped off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: then means subsequently, afterwards

explanation.surface: A fowl later gets beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is a female bird, especially a domestic chicken.

clue.text: City that William tell couldn't have missed!

definitions.text: City that William tell couldn't have missed!

parts.words: City that William tell couldn't have missed!
parts.note: the legendary Swiss archer shot fruit off his son's head; a huge piece of that fruit would be impossible to miss, and it is a nickname of a US city

explanation.surface: A city so large that the famous Swiss marksman could not fail to hit it.
explanation.walkthrough: William Tell is the Swiss folk hero who shot an apple from his son's head; the Big Apple is New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Apple is a popular nickname for New York City.

clue.text: Ferocious person dealt with two sailors

indicators.note: two means the word for sailors is used twice in a row

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A savage individual has dealt with a pair of seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartar is a fierce, violent or intractable person.

clue.text: Cruel sergeant teased American army oficer

indicators.note: teased suggests the letters are pulled apart and combed out into a new order

explanation.surface: A cruel sergeant mocks a US officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teased' rearranges CRUEL SERGEANT. Custer was the US cavalry commander killed at the Little Bighorn in 1876.
explanation.definitionFit: George Armstrong Custer was a US Army commander famous for his last stand at Little Bighorn.
